According to the DMW, the arrest of Mazhoor Ubongin Khusin, also known as Maz, led to the rescue of 1,700 aspiring overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) from falling prey to the recruitment officer’s fake job offers. Khusin allegedly served as an officer of ALJU International Manpower Services, a recruitment agency that had previously faced regulatory sanctions after luring the would-be OFWs to pay excessive placement fees for jobs in Poland, Lithuania and the Czech Republic that were found to be non-existent. The company also failed to refund the applicants of placement fees ranging from P80,000 to P130,000. “The arrest of this illegal recruiter marks a significant development in the cases filed in connection with the recruitment scheme targeting our OFWs who simply want a better life for their families,” DMW Secretary Hans Cacdac said in a statement. The DMW reminded aspiring OFWs to exercise extreme caution when dealing with people who offer jobs overseas, especially when they demand substantial placement fees, promise unusually high salaries or guarantee visas, permanent residency or immediate deployment. https://www.rediff.com/news/report/can-i.text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar highlights Indias continuous diplomatic engagement with both Ukraine and Russia, actively seeking pathways for dialogue and negotiation to mitigate and ultimately cease the ongoing conflict.IMAGE: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar meets Poland deputy Prime Minister RadosÅaw Sikorski, in Warsaw, Poland, September 4, 2026. Photograph: @PolandMFA/ANI PhotoKey PointsIndia actively engages with both Ukrainian and Russian sides to find solutions for conflict mitigation.External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar recently visited Kyiv and Warsaw to discuss global challenges and the Ukraine war.India advocates for dialogue and diplomacy as the primary means to end the prolonged conflict.Prime Minister Narendra Modis public concern about the endless war underscores Indias position.India asserts that trade decisions, such as oil purchases, are separate from diplomatic solutions to the conflict.India has been in continuous touch with both the Ukrainian and Russian sides and is trying to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way that will contribute to the mitigation or the cessation of the conflict, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Friday.Jaishankar, who arrived in Warsaw from Kyiv where he held talks with top Ukrainian leadership on Thursday, made the remarks after he met Polands Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister RadosÅaw Sikorski. Addressing a joint press meet alongside Sikorski, Jaishankar said that he discussed the complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security, with his Polish counterpart.The Deputy Prime Minister and I also understandably discussed some major global and regional issues, notable among them is the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year... I myself have just come here from Kyiv, he said, referring to his visit to Ukraine a day earlier.Indias Diplomatic Engagement In UkraineReplying to a question, he said India has been in continuous touch with both the Ukrainian and Russian sides.What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict, he added.A day earlier, Jaishankar had said in Ukraine that India is ready to extend any help in any manner to end the Ukraine-Russia war.He had met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv on Thursday.After talks with Jaishankar, Zelenskyy had said that he was grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war.Call For Dialogue And DiplomacyThis certainly must not be a time of war. Peace is needed. This is Indias clear position, he said and hoped that other major world powers would also take a clear stance that this war must end and that a reliable peace must be achieved.On Friday, Jaishankar reiterated that India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war.These are wars without winners. Every additional day means more death, more destruction, more loss to the parties themselves, and more cost to the rest of the world, he said in Warsaw.He recalled that this concern was voiced publicly by Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently.Our efforts must therefore focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. We must each do what we can in whichever way we believe could be most effective and support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is Indias strong conviction, and we are acting on it, he added.Trade Not A Solution To ConflictOn Indias purchases of Russian oil, the minister said the issue is a conflict, and its solution lies in negotiations, not in trade.This war is not going to end... not because somebody chose to buy or not buy oil or alumina or fertilisers or metals and minerals. It will end when there is diplomacy, when there is dialogue and when there is negotiation. So, I think lets diagnose the problem right, he said while replying to another question.

R.Power nears completion of its first utility-scale BESS in Romania Energy Investments News Top stories Published on October 12, 2026 By Petre Barac Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email Renewable energy producer R.Power is nearing completion of its first utility-scale BESS project in Romania, the 127MW / 254 MWh Scornicesti BESS. EPC contractor Parapet, working with R.Power’s in-house EPC management team, commenced construction in spring 2026. It has, over the past three months, laid foundations and deployed all 46 battery units and 23 containerised medium-voltage transformer stations. Scornicesti BESS will be one of the first assets of its kind in Romania, and one of the largest BESS assets to enter operation in Central & Eastern Europe (CEE). Connecting Scornicesti directly to the high-voltage national transmission grid, operated by Transelectrica, is a major undertaking that goes well beyond a standard project and has required extensive design works. Once connected, expected in late 2026/early 2027, the project will become a strategic energy asset for Romania’s national energy system. R.Power secured a €46 million financing package for the project in June 2026. Under the terms of the deal, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) provided €44 million in investment and bridge financing, while Polish development bank Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) issued a €2.3 million bank guarantee to secure the long-term optimisation contract in place with regional trading partner GEN-I. The project, located in Olt County, is co-owned through a JV with France’s Eiffel Investment Group. “As a utility-scale asset connected to the national transmission grid, Scornicesti BESS will actively support the stabilisation of Romania’s energy system.” said Florin Federenciuc, R.Power Country Head for Romania . “By integrating BESS at the heart of its energy transition, Romania is strengthening its grid resilience and supporting the roll-out of renewable energy generation. Having contracted our first Romanian PV assets just two years ago, we are proud to now be playing this vital role in one of Europe’s fastest growth energy transition markets. “Together with EBRD, BGK, Eiffel Investment Group and GEN-I, we look forward to completing the final phase of construction and commissioning and getting this strategic asset to work”. Scornicesti BESS forms part of one of Central and Eastern Europe’s largest utility-scale energy storage pipelines. R.Power’s BESS portfolio in operations and under construction in CEE currently stands at 0.9 GW / 3 GWh, with an additional 0.7 GW / 2.8 GWh of commercialised, ready-to-build projects.
